unit-test.description: Create a unit test for a Vue component, composable, or utility in BaseLib
unit-test.template:
Create a complete unit test for the component/composable/utility identified by the name that follows.

## Workflow

1. **Load skills** - Invoke the `unit-testing` skill and `code-style-frontend` skill now
2. **Extract name** - Identify the component/composable/utility name from the remaining user text
3. **Read source** - Find and read the source file (search src/components/*/, src/composables/, src/utils/)
4. **Read 2-3 pattern references** - Read existing test files from similar components:
   - Input fields -> EmailField.spec.ts or PhoneField.spec.ts
   - Buttons -> IconToolTip.spec.ts
   - Overlays -> LoadingOverlay.spec.ts
   - Composables -> useLoading.spec.ts
   - Complex logic -> ZipCodeField.spec.ts or MoneyField.spec.ts
5. **Create the test file** in the correct __tests__/ directory:
   - `src/components/{category}/__tests__/{Name}.spec.ts`
   - `src/composables/__tests__/{name}.spec.ts`
   - `src/utils/__tests__/{name}.spec.ts`
6. **Verify** - Run `pnpm check`; fix any failures

## Mandatory patterns

```ts
import { describe, it, expect, beforeEach, afterEach } from 'vitest';
import { createComponent } from '@/testutils';
import ComponentName from '../ComponentName.vue';

describe('ComponentName', () => {
  let wrapper: ReturnType<typeof createComponent>;

  beforeEach(() => {
    wrapper = createComponent(ComponentName);
  });

  afterEach(() => {
    wrapper.unmount();
  });
});
```

- Use `it.each` with `as const` for repeated cases
- `await wrapper.setProps()` to change props
- `wrapper.find('input').setValue()` and `.trigger()` for input interaction
- `wrapper.emitted('event')` for emitted events
- `wrapper.findComponent({ name: 'v-btn' })` for child Vuetify components
- `wrapper.findAll('.v-messages__message')` for validation messages
- Create helper functions for repeated queries (e.g., `getInputValue()`)

## Prohibited

- NEVER `wrapper.html()` - brittle
- NEVER snapshot tests
- NEVER test Vue/Vuetify internals
- NEVER `any` - type everything
- NEVER `.then().catch()` - always async/await
- NEVER logic in template - computed/methods

## Code style

- Single quotes, semicolons required
- Booleans with is/has/can prefix
- Names in english (variables, functions, describes, its)
- Labels/UI strings in pt-BR
- Early return > ternary > if/else
- Blank line before and after blocks

refactory.description: Refactor a Vue component, composable, or utility to follow BaseLib code-style strictly
refactory.template:
Refactor the component/composable/utility identified by the name that follows to strictly follow BaseLib code standards.

## Workflow

1. **Load skill** - Invoke the `code-style-frontend` skill now
2. **Extract name** - Identify the file name from the remaining user text
3. **Read source** - Find and read the full source file (search src/components/*/, src/composables/, src/utils/)
4. **Read a reference** - Read 1 component that already follows the code style (e.g., EmailField.vue, IconToolTip.vue, useLoading.ts) to understand the target pattern
5. **Read existing test** (if any) - so you don't break the public API
6. **Apply ALL transformations below** - edit the source file in place
7. **Verify** - Run `pnpm check` first, then `pnpm build`; fix any failures

## Code-style transformations (apply ALL)

### Script setup & Composition API
- Ensure `<script setup lang="ts">` (convert Options API if needed)
- Follow the exact order: imports -> interfaces/types -> defineProps/Emits/Slots -> composables -> refs -> computed -> methods -> watch -> lifecycle
- `defineProps` with interface + `withDefaults`
- `defineEmits` typed with `defineEmits<{ event: [payload] }>()`

### Async
- NEVER `.then().catch()` - always `async/await`
- Loading resets in `finally`, never in try or catch

### Conditionals
- Priority: Early Return > Ternary > If/Else
- Nested if/else -> rewrite to early returns
- FORBIDDEN: `switch/case` -> replace with if/ternary/map lookup
- One-line if without braces when single statement
- Blank line before and after `if`/`for`/`while` blocks

### Template
- Zero logic - move conditions to computed (`v-if="computedName"`)
- Boolean props without value: `<v-btn disabled />`
- Extract repeated template chunks to components

### Types & variables
- NEVER `any` - type everything
- Booleans with `is`/`has`/`can` prefix
- Export consumer-facing interfaces/types
- Use `const`/`let`, never `var`

### Strings & formatting
- Single quotes (`'`) always, never double quotes (`"`)
- Semicolons (`;`) required at end of every statement
- `const ITEMS = [...] as const` for constants

### CSS
- NEVER `!important`
- Use Vuetify utility classes instead of custom CSS (d-flex, align-center, pa-4, ga-2, text-body-1, etc.)
- Only write scoped CSS for what Vuetify cannot do (position fixed, transition classes, `:deep()`)

### Names & comments
- Self-documenting - zero comments
- No abreviaturas (`l` -> `labels`, `t` -> `translate`, `fn` -> `format`)
- Variables/functions/tests in english
- Only UI labels in pt-BR

### Library rules (preserve)
- Keep all existing barrel file exports (`src/components/index.ts`, etc.)
- Keep all existing props/emits/slots (do NOT break public API)
- Keep all existing TypeScript interfaces/types that consumers use
- Update existing test if refactor changed behavior
- Keep labels overrideable via props

learn.description: Analyze session diff and update project documentation (ARCHITECTURE.md, COGNITIVE.md, skills) with new patterns and decisions
learn.template:
Analyze the current git diff and update project documentation to reflect new patterns, decisions, and conventions introduced in this session.

## Workflow

1. **Load skills** - Invoke the `code-style-frontend` skill now
2. **Check what changed** - Run `git diff --stat` and `git diff` to see what files were added/modified/deleted. Also check `git diff --cached` for staged changes. Focus on src/ files (not dist/, node_modules/, etc.)
3. **Read current docs** - Read these files in full:
   - `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`
   - `docs/COGNITIVE.md`
   - `.opencode/skills/code-style-frontend/SKILL.md`
   - `.opencode/skills/unit-testing/SKILL.md`
   - `.opencode/skills/code-review/SKILL.md`
4. **Identify new patterns** - From the diff, identify:
   - New directories created (e.g., src/types/, src/constants/)
   - New components, composables, or utilities added
   - New architectural patterns (e.g., provide/inject for defaults)
   - New testing patterns or conventions discovered
   - Design decisions that should be recorded (why was approach X chosen over Y?)
   - Code-style patterns that should be enforced in future sessions
5. **Check for gaps** - For each new pattern, check: is it already documented? If not, it is a gap.
6. **Propose updates** - Show the user a bullet list of proposed doc changes with the exact file and section to update. Ask for approval before editing.
7. **Apply approved updates** - Edit the files following these conventions:
   - `ARCHITECTURE.md` - Add to folder structure, add new sections for new patterns
   - `COGNITIVE.md` - Add numbered decision entry with "What / Why / Trade-offs" format
   - Skills (`SKILL.md`) - Add new rules, patterns, or examples that make the agent more assertive in future sessions
8. **Verify** - Run `pnpm check` to ensure no lint/test regressions

## Doc update conventions

### COGNITIVE.md decision entry format
```
### {N}. {Title}

{1-2 sentences describing what was done}...

pipeline.description: Full pre-merge pipeline: diff, tests, breaking changes, code review, commit/push, and GitHub merge request
pipeline.template:
Run the full pre-merge pipeline for this branch. Follow the workflow defined in the `pipeline` skill.

## Workflow

1. **Load skills** - Invoke the `pipeline`, `code-review`, and `unit-testing` skills now
2. **Git diff analysis** - Fetch main and diff against origin/main to identify all changes
3. **Unit test coverage** - Verify every new/modified src/ file has a corresponding test
4. **Breaking changes detection** - Scan for deleted exports, changed prop types, renamed APIs
5. **Code review** - Run the full code-review checklist against every changed file
6. **Verification** - Run `pnpm lint`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm build` in order; fix any failures
7. **Auto-learning** - Update ARCHITECTURE.md and COGNITIVE.md with new patterns/decisions
8. **Commit and push** - `git add -A`, conventional commit (pt-BR), `git push origin HEAD`
9. **Merge request** - Create MR on GitHub with English description; report URL to user

## Rules
- Fix, don't skip — broken tests/lint must be fixed before proceeding
- Breaking changes must be explicit in the MR description
- Only commit inside this pipeline workflow
